title: The exceptional adjoint on the bounded comparison class
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$, a finite discrete commutative ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(j,p)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], with $\dim\overline X\leq d$ for an integer $d\geq0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and their derived categories on the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $\nu_T^*$ for its exact derived pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Write $F_c=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ for ordinary étale compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $P_c=Rf_{!,n}^c=Rp_*j_!$ for pro-étale compact support at this compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Then:

1. The class-restricted datum [def-sf-fullcd-class] holds for the proper part $p$ with bound $2d$: $\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;2d)$.
2. The functor $F_c$ has a right adjoint $f_c^\times$ on the ordinary étale derived categories. The composite
$$R_cL=\nu_X^*f_c^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L$$
takes bounded-below pro-étale complexes to bounded-below pro-étale complexes. For every bounded-below $K$ of étale origin, meaning there exist $G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], and every $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P_cK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,R_cL).$$
It is independent of the choice of étale-origin witness. Thus $R_c$ is the right adjoint relative to this bounded-below comparison class. This applies in particular to the bounded constructible inputs [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] used here.
3. The compactification comparisons of these functors on the stated domains are canonical and satisfy the cocycle condition; the Hom bijections respect these comparisons.

No adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-étale objects is asserted.

proof.text: The coefficient definition gives that $A$ is a finite commutative ring. The compactification has open $j$ and proper finite-type $p$; since $Y$ is finite type over $k$, so is $\overline X$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,Y,\overline X$ Noetherian. Thus [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] applies to this compactification and supplies $F_c\dashv f_c^\times$ on ordinary unbounded étale $A$-module derived categories. These are precisely the coefficient categories in the statement, without any change to condensed or completed coefficients.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: existence of the ordinary étale right adjoint; unit clause (a) used in clause (c).

proof.text: Apply [thm-sf-fullcd-class] to $p:\overline X\to Y$: both schemes are finite type over the fixed algebraically closed finite-field base, $p$ is proper finite type, the coefficient stage is positive, and $\dim\overline X\leq d$. Its conclusion is exactly $\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;2d)$ of [def-sf-fullcd-class], including the same bound after every pro-étale base change, with original-source étale-origin sheaves pulled back to that base change. This proves clause (1); it makes no assertion for arbitrary pro-étale sheaves.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: Clause (1) is thm-sf-fullcd-class.

proof.text: Here is the global upper-amplitude bound needed in the next step. Apply [lem-kun-relative-torsion-direct-image-dimension-bound] with source $\overline X$, target $Y$, morphism $p$, coefficient ring $A$, and bound $d$. The field $k$ is separably closed, $A$ is finite and hence its additive group is torsion, $p$ is quasi-compact and locally finite type, and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally finite type. Consequently $R^qp_{\mathrm{et},*}M=0$ for every étale $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q>2d$. The module direct image is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact], and its source category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Therefore [lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound] gives $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}D^{\le m}\subseteq D^{\le m+2d}$ for every integer $m$, including complexes unbounded below. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], termwise $j_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ commutes with kernels and cokernels, hence with cohomology, so it preserves $D^{\le m}$. The definition $F_c=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}Dj_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] now gives $F_cD^{\le m}\subseteq D^{\le m+2d}$. The use of the total-derived upper-bound theorem, rather than a bounded-below spectral sequence, is essential here.

source.place: Tag 07K7 (lemma-unbounded-right-derived), (4)(c), applied to the proper part; realizes the blueprint first paragraph finite-cohomological-dimension inference.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-etale-upper-shriek-bounded-below-from-amplitude] to the global bound of Step 3. It follows that the chosen right adjoint preserves $D^+$. The orthogonality argument applies to the adjunction of Step 1 itself, so it gives the conclusion for that chosen adjoint as well. Explicitly, if $H\in D^{\ge a}$ then $f_c^	imes H\in D^{\ge a-2d}$: adjunction tests a morphism from an object of $D^{\le a-2d-1}$ against $H$ after applying $F_c$, where the upper bound is $a-1$. The orthogonality argument is exactly the assertion used from the cited lemma. The bounded-below comparison adjunction of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] sends $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ to $R
u_{Y,*}L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Hence $H_L=f_c^	imes R
u_{Y,*}L$ is bounded below, and the termwise exact pullback of [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] makes $R_cL=
u_X^*H_L$ bounded below. The left functor $F_c$ also sends $D^+$ to $D^+$: exact extension by zero preserves the lower cohomological bound, and a bounded-below injective representative of its output is K-injective, so the unbounded proper direct image and the bounded-below construction of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] are both computed by $p_*$ on that representative.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: f-times preserves bounded-below objects, so all comparison arguments lie in D-plus.

proof.text:
Choose an étale-origin witness $\alpha:
u_X^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ with $G\in D^+$, as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. The natural compact-support comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] and the comparison adjunction in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], followed by the ordinary adjunction of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P_cK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(
u_Y^*F_cG,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_cG,R
u_{Y,*}L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,H_L).$$
Both $G$ and $H_L$ are bounded below by Step 4. Full faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies the last Hom set with $\operatorname{Hom}(
u_X^*G,
u_X^*H_L)$; composition with $\alpha^{-1}$ identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,R_cL)$. Every arrow of this chain is an invertible Hom identification. In particular its final comparison uses full faithfulness at $X$, with no second direct image on the source.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph, displayed Hom chain; unit proof, displayed Hom chain.

proof.text:
For witnesses $(G,\alpha)$ and $(G',\alpha')$ of $K$, full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives a unique isomorphism $u:G	o G'$ with $
u_X^*u=\alpha'^{-1}\alpha$ (lift the inverse as well, and use faithfulness). Naturality in the witness of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] and naturality of the two adjunction bijections imply that the intermediate maps $b:G	o H_L$ and $b':G'	o H_L$ obtained in Step 5 satisfy $b=b'u$. Thus $
u_X^*b\,\alpha^{-1}=
u_X^*b'\,\alpha'^{-1}$, proving independence of the witness. Write $\Phi_{c,K,L}$ for the resulting bijection. For a morphism $v:K	o K'$ with witnesses $(G,\alpha)$ and $(G',\alpha')$, lift $\alpha'^{-1}v\alpha$ uniquely to $u:G	o G'$. If $h:P_cK'	o L$ corresponds to $b':G'	o H_L$, naturality of the compact-support comparison and the adjunctions says that $h\circ P_c(v)$ corresponds to $b'u$. Since $
u_X^*u\circ\alpha^{-1}=\alpha'^{-1}\circ v$, this gives $\Phi_{c,K,L}(h\circ P_c(v))=\Phi_{c,K',L}(h)\circ v$. For $h:P_cK	o L$ and $w:L	o L'$, the intermediate map for $w\circ h$ is $f_c^	imes R
u_{Y,*}(w)\circ b$, where $b$ is that for $h$; hence $\Phi_{c,K,L'}(w\circ h)=R_c(w)\circ\Phi_{c,K,L}(h)$. Therefore Step 5 gives the claimed natural relative adjunction.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: the bijection is natural and independent of the witness.

proof.text: By clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], every bounded constructible pro-étale complex has a bounded constructible étale representative and in particular a bounded-below étale-origin witness. Bounded constructible target complexes are bounded below. Hence Step 5 applies to the bounded constructible inputs of the statement. This uses only the inclusion of the bounded constructible class in étale origin, not an identification of all étale-origin sheaves with constructible sheaves.

source.place: Unit proof, final sentence (Stacks Tag 09AK); item clause (2), last sentence.

proof.text:
For compactifications $c,c'$, let $e_{c,c'}:F_c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c'}$ on $D^+$ be the canonical comparison of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. For $K=
u_X^*G$ let $a_c(G):P_c
u_X^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_Y^*F_cG$ be [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Define the comparison on this class by
$$t_{c,c'}(
u_X^*G)=a_{c'}(G)^{-1}\circ
u_Y^*(e_{c,c'}(G))\circ a_c(G).$$
For a general witness $\alpha:
u_X^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, conjugate by $P_c\alpha$ and $P_{c'}\alpha$. For $u:G	o G'$, the two naturality equations are $a_c(G')\circ P_c(
u_X^*u)=
u_Y^*(F_cu)\circ a_c(G)$ and $e_{c,c'}(G')\circ F_cu=F_{c'}u\circ e_{c,c'}(G)$. Substitution in the displayed formula gives $t_{c,c'}(
u_X^*G')\circ P_c(
u_X^*u)=P_{c'}(
u_X^*u)\circ t_{c,c'}(
u_X^*G)$. For witnesses $(G,\alpha)$ of $K$ and $(G',\alpha')$ of $K'$ and a map $v:K	o K'$, full faithfulness lifts $\alpha'^{-1}v\alpha$ to such a $u$. Conjugating this equation gives naturality in $v$, and taking $v=1_K$ proves independence of the witness. The identities $e_{c,c}=1$ and $e_{c',c''}e_{c,c'}=e_{c,c''}$ give $t_{c,c}=1$ and $t_{c',c''}t_{c,c'}=t_{c,c''}$ by cancellation of $a_{c'}a_{c'}^{-1}$. Thus the lower-functor comparisons, normalized by the canonical étale comparison, are canonical and satisfy the cocycle condition.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: transport canonical coherent étale compactification comparisons through the fixed comparison functors.

proof.text:
For any other compactification $c'$, its middle scheme is finite type over $k$, so [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives a finite nonnegative dimension bound (use $0$ for the empty scheme). Write $c'=(j',p')$ and choose this bound $d'$. Finite-type permanence as in Step 1 makes its middle scheme Noetherian, so [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] supplies $F_{c'}\dashv f_{c'}^	imes$. Apply [lem-kun-relative-torsion-direct-image-dimension-bound] to $p'$ over the same separably closed field with the same torsion coefficient ring $A$: properness gives quasi-compactness, $p'$ is locally of finite type, and its source has dimension at most $d'$. Thus $R^qp'_*M=0$ for all module sheaves and $q>2d'$. The left exactness and enough-injectives statements used in Step 3 apply to this source as well [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Therefore [lem-sf-finite-cd-derived-upper-bound], followed by exact $j'_!$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], gives $F_{c'}D^{\le m}\subset D^{\le m+2d'}$. Now [lem-etale-upper-shriek-bounded-below-from-amplitude] proves preservation of $D^+$ for $f_{c'}^	imes$. The bound need not equal $d$, which is used only for clause (1) at the original compactification. For bounded-below étale $H$, these facts make $f_c^	imes H$ and $f_{c'}^	imes H$ objects of $D^+$. Precomposition with $e_{c,c'}$ and the two étale adjunctions give a natural isomorphism between the functors $G\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(G,f_{c'}^	imes H)$ and $G\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(G,f_c^	imes H)$ on $D^+$. Evaluate it at the identity of $f_{c'}^	imes H$ to get $b_{c,c'}(H):f_{c'}^	imes H	o f_c^	imes H$. Naturality implies that every component of that Hom transformation is postcomposition with $b_{c,c'}(H)$. Evaluating the inverse transformation at the other identity shows that these maps are inverse isomorphisms. This also proves uniqueness. More explicitly, if $J^c_{G,H}:\operatorname{Hom}(F_cG,H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(G,f_c^	imes H)$ is the chosen étale adjunction bijection, the normalization is
$$J^c_{G,H}(z\circ e_{c,c'}(G))=b_{c,c'}(H)\circ J^{c'}_{G,H}(z).$$
Naturality of $J$ in $H$ gives $b_{c,c'}(H')\circ f_{c'}^	imes(w)=f_c^	imes(w)\circ b_{c,c'}(H)$ for $w:H	o H'$. The equations $e_{c,c}=1$ and $e_{c',c''}e_{c,c'}=e_{c,c''}$ in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], substituted into the normalization, give $b_{c,c}=1$ and $b_{c,c'}b_{c',c''}=b_{c,c''}$ by evaluation at identities. Apply the fixed functors $R
u_{Y,*}$ and $
u_X^*$ to obtain the canonical comparisons $R_{c'}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_c$. For $h:P_{c'}K	o L$, the compatibility required of the Hom bijections is the explicit equation
$$\Phi_{c,K,L}(h\circ t_{c,c'}(K))=
u_X^*b_{c,c'}(R
u_{Y,*}L)\circ\Phi_{c',K,L}(h).$$
On a representative $K=
u_X^*G$ the equation $a_{c'}(G)t_{c,c'}(K)=
u_Y^*e_{c,c'}(G)a_c(G)$ first turns the left side into precomposition by $
u_Y^*e_{c,c'}(G)$. Naturality of the comparison adjunction turns this into precomposition by $e_{c,c'}(G)$; the normalization of $J$ above then turns it into postcomposition by $b_{c,c'}(R
u_{Y,*}L)$. Applying full faithfulness gives the displayed equation, and conjugating by a general witness gives it for $K$. Thus the relative adjunctions respect the comparisons. No right-adjoint assertion outside $D^+$, and no unbounded pro-étale compactification comparison, was used.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type over $\Fbar$, with a
compactification of dimension at most $d$, and let $A=A_{E,n}$.
Then the following statements hold:

1. The class-restricted dimension datum
[def-sf-fullcd-class] holds with bound $2d$.
1. Let $f^\times$ be the right adjoint of the étale
compact-support functor. On bounded-below pro-étale coefficients put
$$
Rf_n^\times L=\nu_X^* f^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L.
$$
For every bounded-below $K$ of étale origin and every bounded-below
$L$, there is a natural bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,n}K,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,Rf_n^\times L).
$$
Thus this formula is the right adjoint relative to the bounded-below
comparison class.
1. Compactification comparisons of these functors are canonical and
satisfy the cocycle condition.

No adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-étale objects is asserted.

proof.text:
Clause (1) is [thm-sf-fullcd-class]. Write $K=\nu_X^*G$ with
$G$ bounded below. The finite cohomological dimension of compact
support implies that its right adjoint $f^\times$ takes bounded-below
objects to bounded-below objects: a bound
$Rf_!D^{\leq0}\subseteq D^{\leq N}$ gives
$f^\times D^{\geq0}\subseteq D^{\geq-N}$ by adjunction and
orthogonality. Hence all étale objects in the following comparison
are in the domain of the fully faithful functor of
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Using
[lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] and the adjoint of
[thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] gives

$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,n}\nu_X^*G,L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!^{\Et}G,R\nu_{Y,*}L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,f^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\nu_X^*G,\nu_X^*f^\times R\nu_{Y,*}L).
$$

The last step is full faithfulness, not an adjunction with a second
$R\nu_{X,*}$; the latter would have the wrong source category.
The bijection is natural and independent of the witness. The coherent
compactification comparisons follow by applying the fixed functors
$\nu_X^*$ and $R\nu_{Y,*}$ to the étale comparisons of
[lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] and using uniqueness of the
étale right adjoints. This proves (2) and (3).
